facts.detail: Ofcom last updated its bill-payment difficulty guidance on 8 April 2026.
Customers having difficulty paying are advised to contact their provider as soon as possible.
Potential options include a cheaper package, repayment over time, reduced monthly payments or a changed payment date.
The guidance states that providers are not obliged to offer the suggested payment arrangements.
Continued missed payments may lead to service restriction or disconnection, with extra contact expected for some vulnerable customers.

guard_streams.source: Broadband and landline faults and problems

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the broadband and landline faults guide on 8 April 2026.
Home wiring changes, extension leads and missing or unsuitable microfilters can reduce broadband performance.
Older routers or outdated software can cause connection problems and may need replacement or updating.
Providers may diagnose faults remotely or request Ethernet and line-speed tests.
An unresolved complaint can be referred to ADR after six weeks or earlier with a deadlock letter.

guard_streams.source: Are you in or out of contract?

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated its in-or-out-of-contract guidance on 17 July 2026.
Phone, broadband and pay-TV contracts commonly use 12, 18 or 24-month minimum periods.
Leaving before the minimum period ends may trigger an early termination charge.
Providers must send an end-of-contract notification between 10 and 40 days before the contract ends.
The notification must include the end date, notice period, current and post-contract prices, best deals and relevant bundled-contract details.
